assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear chain from theory to measurement: the quantum spin Hall state (predicted theoretically, observed in HgTe quantum wells) and the quantum anomalous Hall effect (observed in magnetic topological insulator films). It created a new classification of matter with a topological bulk-boundary structure, with wide influence on materials and theory. This is a discovery in nature rather than only a formalism.
assessment.attribution: Kane is the decisive theorist on the Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall idea; Molenkamp led the HgTe experiment that confirmed the quantum spin Hall edge transport; Xue led the experimental quantum anomalous Hall realization. This three-person set is coherent. Other contributors, such as the HgTe-well prediction and the Haldane model, may deserve recognition, but they are not credited names here, so I cannot propose them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple independent groups across more than fifteen years, with the interpretation stable and the field mature. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Which theory contributions must be recognized beside Kane is unsettled, and the supplied credit set may omit key theorists; I cannot verify this from the list alone.
The quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects are separate discoveries, and a prize may need to decide how far to bundle them.
Overlap with the separate B013 and B029 entries means the framing of the prize is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which flat bands produce correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system. The theoretical flat-band prediction was followed by striking experimental discovery. It has had very large, rapid impact and spawned a whole field of moire physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated insulator and superconductivity. That is a natural theory plus experiment trio. Andrei's earlier work on twisted-bilayer electronic structure is a competing claim whose weight I cannot settle from the supplied evidence.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups since 2018 and robust as a phenomenon. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, which makes the timing slightly early, though the discovery of the effects is secure.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Allocation of credit between Andrei and others, and the role of earlier twisted-bilayer theory, is not clear from the supplied credit.
Only about eight years since the experiments, so some committee members may find it premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains horizon, flatness and the origin of primordial fluctuations, and its quantum-fluctuation predictions of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum agree with CMB and large-scale-structure data. As a theorist I find the idea deeply important, though the lasting impact depends on how well the specific inflationary mechanism is established.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed inflation and Linde (new inflation, chaotic inflation) made it a workable theory; Mukhanov gave the quantum origin of structure. Starobinsky's pioneering contribution, and Albrecht and Steinhardt's, complicate any three-person division, and I cannot rule out that the supplied names leave out essential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The qualitative predictions of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum are strongly supported, but there is no direct evidence for primordial gravitational waves or for a specific inflaton, and the alternatives are not fully excluded. Prize timing is defensible but empirically incomplete.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes; the inflationary mechanism remains unproven.
Attribution is contested and may leave out Starobinsky and others.
I recall the Nobel tradition preferring empirical confirmation, so this may be considered theoretical and premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened neutrino astronomy and created a new observational window, including a blazar association and later Galactic-plane evidence. This is clearly a discovery of nature and an instrument at the very frontier.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, and a single-laureate prize is possible. The collaboration is very large and the instrument was built over decades by many people, so crediting a single person is a real simplification; other leaders may merit consideration but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed independently and the blazar and Galactic associations are supported but still few in number. Recognition is timely and moving toward maturity.
uncertainties: Source identification is limited to a few objects.
A single-person credit for a large collaboration can be seen as unfair.
I cannot independently verify the detailed leadership history of the project.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows settled the long-standing origin question by showing that bursts are cosmological and enormously energetic. It opened a whole era of multiwavelength transient astronomy. Importance and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow detection; Kulkarni's group provided the optical and radio follow-up and redshift identification. That gives a balanced experiment-observation split, though Paczynski and others (the late) and van Paradijs and the redshift teams complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Mature after nearly thirty years of confirmation, with the cosmological origin and the supernova connection well established. Timing is more than ripe, perhaps late.
uncertainties: Several key people are deceased or not in the credit set, so a fair division is hard.
Competing roles of the optical teams and the BeppoSAX team need careful weighing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurement of the third mixing angle theta13 was decisive for the three-flavor picture and made CP violation in the lepton sector experimentally accessible. It is a clean, important, particle-physics discovery that completed a measurement set.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) reported a definitive non-zero value from reactor disappearance; T2K (Nishikawa) reported electron-neutrino appearance. RENO and Double Chooz were parallel efforts and are not in this credit set, so the allocation has a clear problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent reactor and accelerator experiments and now measured with percent-level precision; timing is fine, but the prize for neutrino oscillations was already awarded in 2015, which may reduce its priority.
uncertainties: Competition among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K means attribution is unresolved.
The discovery may be seen as a continuation of the already-recognized oscillation work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The AdS/CFT correspondence is among the most influential ideas in theoretical physics and has reshaped quantum gravity, strongly coupled field theory and black-hole physics. I know this field well, and its conceptual importance is unquestionable. But a Nobel prize in physics has generally rested on a link to nature, and I note that the correspondence is a conjecture with extensive consistency checks rather than a verified description of our universe.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena proposed the duality; Witten and, separately, Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov developed the dictionary. Polyakov is credited here but his role is more through the later formulation, and Gubser, who died in 2019, and Klebanov are not in the list. I propose Maldacena and Witten as the clearest pair.
assessment.maturity: Heavily tested internally and applied to heavy-ion and condensed-matter systems, but without a decisive experimental confirmation of the principle itself. As a string theorist I should declare that my own field's interest could make me overvalue it.
uncertainties: No direct empirical test of the gravity side; relevance to real-world systems is by analogy.
Attribution among Maldacena, Witten, Polyakov, Gubser and Klebanov is unresolved.
My professional proximity to this field is a bias risk.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation peak, detected in galaxy clustering, gave a robust standard ruler for cosmic expansion and underpins current dark-energy and geometry measurements. The discovery was a clear and important empirical feature that links early-universe physics to late-time observations.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein and the SDSS team and the 2dFGRS team (Cole, Percival) made independent detections in 2005, a natural pair of groups, though the leadership of large survey collaborations is spread among many people and the theory credit (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) is outside this list.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many later surveys including BOSS and DESI, which is a strong sign of maturity. Hints of tension in recent dark-energy results add current interest but do not weaken the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Collaboration credit is diffuse and a three-person selection may be arbitrary.
Earlier theoretical work on acoustic peaks is not included in the credited names, and Peebles has already been recognized in 2019.
